name: beagle
desc: Evaluate the likelihood of sequence evolution on trees
why: A high-performance library for computing sequence evolution likelihoods on phylogenetic trees, real science you can run.

brief.what_it_is: BEAGLE is a high-performance library for evaluating phylogenetic likelihoods, meaning continuous-time Markov models of biomolecular sequence evolution on trees. Phylogenetics software passes it the model and sequence data, and it returns likelihood values. It can run the calculations on highly parallel hardware such as GPUs in ordinary PCs. It is a library with an open API, not a standalone command-line program.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the aim is to provide high-performance evaluation 'services' to a wide range of phylogenetic software, both Bayesian samplers and Maximum Likelihood optimizers, so those packages can use optimized hardware such as GPUs without each implementing it themselves.
brief.how_it_works: Host programs such as BEAST, BEAST2, and MrBayes call the BEAGLE API to perform the core likelihood calculations, and BEAGLE dispatches them to optimized implementations, including GPU ones. The README links a paper describing the algorithms for computing sequence likelihoods on trees with many-core devices. It does not go into more detail on the mechanism.
brief.install_notes: The README offers binary installers for macOS (v4.0.0, universal, Darwin x86 and ARM) and Windows 64-bit (v4.0.0 .msi), plus older v3.1.0 installers for macOS with CUDA and Windows. Separate wiki pages cover installation on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and the Linux page was not opened. The README mentions no account, runtime, or configuration step. Code signing is provided free by SignPath.io. The README does not say whether a CUDA or other GPU driver is needed for GPU use, so check the install wiki.
brief.standout: Rather than being a phylogenetics package itself, BEAGLE is shared infrastructure: one API that several major Bayesian and maximum-likelihood programs call so they can run the same likelihood math on GPUs.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the README shows: the current binaries are v4.0.0, and the README lists both current and previous installers with release-download links. I did not see a release date or last-commit date on the fetched page, so I cannot confirm recency from this page alone.
brief.caveats: It is a library, not a user-facing tool, so you cannot run it directly and it has no commands. The README says support for several packages (Garli, PhyML, RevBayes, PAUP*) is experimental or in development, and BEAST, BEAST2, and MrBayes are the only ones listed as using it now. GPU support depends on the hardware and drivers available, and the README does not detail those requirements. The README does not state a license in the portion I read.
quotes: BEAGLE is a high-performance library that can perform the core calculations at the heart of most Bayesian and Maximum Likelihood phylogenetics packages.
The aim is to provide high performance evaluation 'services' to a wide range of phylogenetic software, both Bayesian samplers and Maximum Likelihood optimizers.
